claims.statement: Bremelanotide, marketed as Vyleesi, is FDA-approved as a melanocortin receptor agonist indicated for the treatment of premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD); the label explicitly states it is not indicated for HSDD in postmenopausal women or in men, and not indicated to enhance sexual performance.

claims.statement: In FDA-approved labeling, nausea was reported by 40% of patients receiving up to 8 monthly doses of Vyleesi, requiring anti-emetic therapy in 13% of patients; focal hyperpigmentation (face, gingiva, breasts) was reported by 1% of patients receiving up to 8 doses per month, and the label states resolution of this hyperpigmentation was not confirmed in all patients after discontinuation -- i.e. it may be permanent in some patients. The RECONNECT phase 3 trials separately reported nausea, flushing, and headache each occurring in 10% or more of bremelanotide-treated patients versus placebo, mostly mild to moderate in intensity.

context.population: premenopausal women with HSDD treated in clinical trials and post-approval labeling review
context.doseText: up to 8 doses per month (label-reported exposure, not a use recommendation)

claims.statement: Bremelanotide is a synthetic cyclic heptapeptide melanocortin receptor agonist (active metabolite of the earlier candidate melanotan II) that engages several melanocortin receptors, predominantly MC4R (implicated in central regulation of sexual arousal/desire pathways) and MC1R (implicated in skin pigmentation, the accepted mechanistic explanation for the focal hyperpigmentation adverse effect documented elsewhere in this packet).

extractedEvidence.quote: VYLEESI is a melanocortin receptor agonist indicated for the treatment of premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD)
Bremelanotide engages several melanocortin receptors (MCR), predominantly MC1R and MC4R, the latter of which is believed to modulate sexual desire.

reviewFlags: Remediation 2026-08-29: receptor-subtype specificity independently confirmed via NCBI Bookshelf (structured clinical reference, independent of DailyMed/DrugBank); statement updated to name MC1R alongside MC4R since MC1R engagement explains the hyperpigmentation adverse effect.

claims.statement: In two identical phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (RECONNECT; total 1,267 premenopausal women with HSDD randomized, 1,202 in the efficacy population), as-needed subcutaneous bremelanotide 1.75 mg over 24 weeks produced statistically significant improvements versus placebo on both co-primary endpoints: increase in Female Sexual Function Index-desire domain score (Study 301: +0.30, P<.001; Study 302: +0.42, P<.001) and reduction in Female Sexual Distress Scale-Desire/Arousal/Orgasm score (Study 301: -0.37, P<.001; Study 302: -0.29, P=.005). An independent published reanalysis of the same trials found that a majority of protocol-listed outcomes were not reported in the original publication and that participants showed a preference for placebo over bremelanotide when offered the choice to continue treatment; these co-primary results should be read alongside that tolerability/preference context rather than in isolation.

context.population: premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD (n=1,267 randomized)
context.doseText: 1.75 mg subcutaneously as needed, over a 24-week trial period (trial protocol description; not a use recommendation)

extractedEvidence.quote: Female Sexual Function Index-desire domain: Bremelanotide showed statistically significant increases compared to placebo across both studies (Study 301: 0.30, P<.001; Study 302: 0.42, P<.001; integrated: 0.35, P<.001)
Female Sexual Distress Scale: Significant reductions in distress (Study 301: -0.37, P<.001; Study 302: -0.29, P=.005; integrated: -0.33, P<.001)
72.72% of protocol-listed outcomes were not reported
participants showed preference for placebo over the drug treatment

reviewFlags: effect sizes are modest on validated instrument scales; clinical-meaningfulness interpretation should not be overstated

Remediation 2026-08-29: independently confirmed via Spielmans 2021 (Journal of Sex Research reanalysis, a source family independent of the original Kingsberg RCT report) that ~73% of protocol-prespecified outcomes went unreported and that participants preferred placebo when given the choice to continue; statement updated to disclose this tolerability/preference context alongside the favorable co-primary results.

The more granular figures cited in the independent-review finding (exact open-label-extension continuation rates by arm, and the specific magnitude of the AE-driven dropout differential) were not independently re-verified against a fetched primary source this session (Europe PMC and the publisher page were unreachable/paywalled); those specific figures remain unconfirmed and are not asserted in this statement -- see ops.reviewReasons.

claims.statement: Only the FDA-approved subcutaneous autoinjector form (Vyleesi, 1.75 mg) has controlled human efficacy and safety data supporting the HSDD indication. Intranasal PT-141/bremelanotide was studied in early-phase, published controlled human trials from the original pre-Vyleesi development program (e.g., a placebo-controlled dose/pharmacodynamic study in men with erectile dysfunction, including co-administration with sildenafil); the intranasal route was where the drug's transient blood-pressure/heart-rate signal was first characterized, which is part of why later development shifted to the subcutaneous route used in Vyleesi. That early intranasal research does not establish safety or efficacy for today's unregulated compounded PT-141 nasal spray products sold online (commonly 1-2 mg per spray, per vendor marketing): those products are not FDA-approved formulations, are untested at their marketed concentrations, and are not supported by the RECONNECT trial evidence, which tested only the subcutaneous route. A vendor page explicitly frames intranasal PT-141 as 'off-label' even while acknowledging Vyleesi's approval status.

context.population: consumers/patients seeking PT-141 outside the approved indication or route
context.formulation: compounded PT-141 nasal spray, various vendor concentrations
context.useCase: off-label/unapproved-formulation use marketed for libido or general sexual enhancement

extractedEvidence.quote: PT-141 (bremelanotide) is FDA-approved as Vyleesi for premenopausal women with HSDD. Compounded intranasal use is off-label and requires a prescription.
Compounded intranasal PT-141 is commonly prepared at 1 mg to 2 mg per spray
VYLEESI is a melanocortin receptor agonist indicated for the treatment of premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD)

Co-administration of low doses of intranasal PT-141, a melanocortin receptor agonist, and sildenafil to men with erectile dysfunction results in an enhanced erectile response; the erectile response induced by co-administration of PT-141 and sildenafil was significantly greater than sildenafil alone, with no increased adverse events.

reviewFlags: misinformation-adjacent: vendor marketing extrapolates an approved subcutaneous product's evidence to an unapproved intranasal route and broader 'sexual enhancement' framing not supported by the label, which explicitly excludes performance-enhancement use

Remediation 2026-08-29: the packet's original reviewFlag stating 'no controlled human trial for intranasal PT-141 was located' was inaccurate. Independently confirmed (Europe PMC, source family independent of the vendor page and label) that published early-phase human trials of intranasal PT-141 exist from the original Palatin development program (Diamond et al. 2005, PMID 15833522). Statement corrected from an absence-of-evidence claim to an accurate description: early intranasal human data exist but do not validate current unregulated compounded products.

A separate reviewer-cited intranasal trial in women (Safarinejad 2008, PMID 18179455) was reported by the independent reviewer as later formally retracted; this session made a targeted attempt to independently verify that retraction status (Europe PMC REST, Semantic Scholar API, Crossref) but all routes were rate-limited or unreachable before confirmation, so the retraction claim is NOT included in the statement above and remains unverified -- see ops.reviewReasons.
